usages.explain: Used in conversations. It's not used to indicate causality, but rather to make the listener understand the speaker's intention, as in "What I mean is this...", when there is disagreement between two people's opinions,... Because this way of speaking strongly asserts one's determination, it often carries a rude sense, seeming to force others.

examples.content: A: お腹が痛いんだ。B: だから、言ったでしょ。まだ沸騰していない水は絶対飲んではいけないって。
examples.transcription: A: おはらがいたいんだ。B: だから、いったでしょ。まだふっとうしていないみずはぜったいのんではいけないって。
examples.mean: A: My stomach hurts. B: That's why I said it. Never drink water that has not yet boiled.

usages.synopsis: This is a way of speaking that strongly expresses one's assertion, so it often contains rude meanings and seems to force others.

title: だから => Well (I told you) ... that's it (Affirmative)
